name: conviction-gated-rebalance
rationale: Literature-motivated (arXiv:2606.00060). Every turnover mechanism this pipeline has tested gates on the POSITION GAP or on the CLOCK: `allocation_threshold` and `boundary-rebalance-no-trade-band` gate on |target - current|, `rebalance-spacing-15m` and the two `post-trade-cooldown-*` variants gate on elapsed time, `h6-block-held-signal` gates on how often the composite may change. None has ever gated on the SIGNAL'S OWN CONVICTION — how far the composite sits from neutral at the moment the trade would be placed. The paper's central finding is exactly that gap: on 70,128 hourly BTC bars with a 10bp all-in cost and a 27-fold walk-forward protocol, naive sign-following collapsed from +73.5% gross to -64.0% net on 10,619 trades, and the single intervention that rescued it was refusing to act on forecasts too weak to pay for their own turnover (positions update only when the forecast magnitude exceeds lambda * cost * |position change|, lambda = 2.0), which cut trades from ~10,600 to 251 (-97.6%) and took the long-only strategy to +65.4% net at Sharpe 1.09. shirube has no return forecast to put in that inequality, but it has the composite's distance from neutral as a conviction proxy, and the failure mode the paper describes is precisely shirube's: the 2026-09-17 baseline loses 4.16pp of return and 6.81 of Sharpe to a one-trade static mix while paying 2.58% of capital in fees, and yesterday's `h6-block-held-signal` established that slowing the signal 271x moved the result sharply toward the static mix from below — i.e. the loss is concentrated in low-information signal churn. This hypothesis is also the mandatory cost-targeting hypothesis for this run (the baseline's `sharpe_minus_static_mix` is now negative for a FOURTH consecutive run: -2.7158, -1.3154, -4.2352, -6.8143), so per the doc's cost caveat it must be scored on `total_fees_jpy` and `traded_volume_jpy`, never on trade count. A specific reason to expect it to survive the trade-count floor where yesterday's three variants did not: at the 50,000 JPY promotion capital the 0.001 BTC lot floor already requires roughly 0.245 allocation units of gap before any order is placed, which under the baseline zone slope of 1.25 corresponds to a composite excursion of ~0.196 — far larger than the 0.06 gate proposed here — so the gate should mostly suppress the mid-band churn that dominates turnover at 500,000 JPY while leaving the large, lot-clearing swings at 50,000 JPY intact. If that reasoning is right the variant keeps its trade count at the deciding capital and is scoreable; if it is wrong, the run measures how much of the primary capital's turnover is low-conviction, which is itself the number lead #1 needs.
code_change_summary: Refuse to place a rebalancing order while the composite signal sits too close to neutral, leaving every other mechanism byte-identical. Three coupled changes, NONE of which touch TradingEngine::compute_btc_target. (1) src/config.rs: add `pub min_conviction: f64` to TradingConfig with `#[serde(default = "default_min_conviction")]` returning 0.0, where 0.0 means 'no gate' — note the gate is written as a STRICT comparison `(composite - 0.5).abs() < cfg.min_conviction`, so 0.0 can never suppress anything and the default is an exact no-op with no IEEE-754 identity hazard (contrast the 2026-09-16 `damped-composite-exposure` finding, where an arithmetic identity was not bitwise exact). Set it to 0.0 in TradingConfig::default(). Extend TradingConfig::validate() to require it to be finite and within [0.0, 0.5], with a Japanese error message matching the style of the surrounding messages. Add a unit test that a config JSON WITHOUT the field deserialises to 0.0, and confirm the DB round-trip in src/storage/config.rs still works (the repository serialises the whole struct as JSON, so a serde default suffices). (2) src/trading/engine.rs: add one new pure associated function, `pub(crate) fn conviction(normalized: f64) -> f64`, returning `(normalized - 0.5).abs()` — the composite's distance from the neutral point. Document it with the formula, its range [0.0, 0.5] for a composite in [0,1], the fact that 0.5 is the neutral point that `compute_btc_target` centres on, and a NOTE citing this hypothesis and arXiv:2606.00060's cost-justified-threshold rule. (3) Gate the ORDER path — and only the order path — on that conviction at BOTH sites. In src/backtest/simulator.rs::run, carry a `last_conviction: Option<f64>` next to the existing `sticky_target`, updated on exactly the same candles on which `sticky_target` is updated (i.e. whenever compute_btc_target returns Some; when it returns None the previous conviction is PRESERVED, mirroring the sticky_target semantics) and consulted at the point where `rebalance_due` and `sticky_target` currently decide whether to evaluate the allocation delta: when `cfg.min_conviction > 0.0` and `last_conviction` is `Some(c)` with `c < cfg.min_conviction`, skip the allocation-delta evaluation for that candle entirely. In src/trading/engine.rs, carry the same `last_conviction` field on TradingEngine, set it in handle_indicator on exactly the branch that updates `sticky_target`, and apply the identical gate on the order-submission path used by BOTH handle_indicator and the periodic rebalance handler (around line 501, `handle_rebalance`), so a low-conviction composite cannot be acted on through the drift path either. EVERYTHING ELSE MUST KEEP RUNNING ON EVERY CANDLE/SIGNAL: the ticker update, compute_btc_target, the sticky_target update, risk_manager.observe_time, the circuit-breaker check, and the rebalance_interval_secs spacing bookkeeping — only the allocation-delta evaluation is suppressed, exactly as the enabling fix for `rebalance-spacing-15m` scoped its own skip. Add unit tests covering: conviction(0.5) == 0.0; conviction(0.0) == conviction(1.0) == 0.5; the gate is inert at min_conviction = 0.0 for a composite exactly at 0.5; a composite 0.03 from neutral is suppressed at min_conviction = 0.06 and acted on at 0.02; and a simulator-level test that a large min_conviction produces strictly fewer trades than 0.0 over the same candles while 0.0 is unchanged. In your report, state the distribution of |composite - 0.5| over the evaluated candles (min/median/max and the fraction below 0.06), how many allocation-delta evaluations the gate suppressed, and `orders_below_min` plus `total_fees_jpy` and `traded_volume_jpy` at all three capitals, so the turnover reduction can be attributed to the gate rather than to the lot floor.
constraints: MUST NOT change TradingEngine::compute_btc_target's signature (its parameter list or return type) or its body — this hypothesis gates on that function's RESULT, so the composite formula is held fixed and the measured effect is attributable to the gate alone.

MUST apply the gate at BOTH call sites (the live sites in src/trading/engine.rs — handle_indicator AND the periodic rebalance handler — and the backtest site in src/backtest/simulator.rs::run), so the backtest cannot measure a strategy the live engine would not run. Leaving the live path unchanged would make the backtest result meaningless.

MUST default `min_conviction` to 0.0 via serde and in TradingConfig::default(), and MUST write the gate as a strict `<` comparison so 0.0 is an exact no-op. The baseline run must remain byte-identical to a run of the unmodified code — verify this explicitly (hash or diff the three-capital reports before and after your change) and say so in your report before quoting any variant number.

MUST NOT change TradingEngine::allocation_delta_to_order, the allocation_threshold comparison at any call site, apply_zone, the sticky_target semantics, the rebalance_interval_secs spacing logic, the RiskManager call sequence, the exchange lot-size check, the fee logic, or the orders_below_min counting arm.
MUST preserve the previous conviction when compute_btc_target returns None, mirroring sticky_target — a warmup or all-neutral IndicatorPoint must not silently unlock or lock the gate.

MUST pass `cargo test`, including the existing compute_btc_target_* tests in src/trading/engine.rs and the simulator tests in src/backtest/simulator.rs — update an expected value only where the new field legitimately changes it (do not weaken or delete a test just to make it pass).

A promoted change still becomes its own PR against dev (per the pipeline's step 6) and is never merged automatically — a human reviews it like any other algorithm hypothesis. Flag explicitly in the PR description that this diff suppresses order submission on the LIVE order-submission path, per the 'anything touching live trading behavior gets flagged explicitly' rule in docs/self-improvement-loop.md.
MUST NOT touch src/exchange/bitflyer/*, .github/workflows/*, or the bitFlyer REST/WS client.

paper_reference.title: Machine Learning-Based Bitcoin Trading Under Transaction Costs: Evidence From Walk-Forward Forecasting
paper_reference.key_claim: On hourly BTC, forecast-following strategies are destroyed by their own turnover (XGBoost long-only: +73.50% gross, -64.00% net on 10,619 trades at 10bp), and the intervention that rescues them is a cost-justified execution filter — update the position only when the forecast magnitude exceeds lambda * cost * |position change| (lambda = 2.0) — which cuts trades 97.6% to 251 and yields +65.40% annual at Sharpe 1.09.
paper_reference.pros: Same asset, same approximate bar frequency regime (hourly vs shirube's 1-minute bars, both far faster than any horizon where TA edge is usually claimed), an all-in 10bp cost close to shirube's 12.8bp effective rate at the promotion capital, and a genuinely serious out-of-sample design (27-fold walk-forward, 12m train / 3m validate / 3m test, features and scaling refit inside each fold, 2018-2026). Its diagnosis matches shirube's measured condition almost exactly: a strategy with plausible gross behaviour whose net result is dominated by turnover, losing to buy-and-hold. And its remedy is a mechanism shirube has never tested — gating on the signal's own strength rather than on the position gap or the clock — so it adds a new axis rather than re-testing a rejected one.
paper_reference.cons: Do not trust the numbers. The instrument is BTC/USDT PERPETUAL FUTURES with a long-short mode, not BTC/JPY spot long-only, and the headline +65.40% comes from a strategy whose maximum drawdown is -67.42%, which shirube's risk gates would never permit. More importantly the filter is defined on a supervised RETURN FORECAST with a calibrated magnitude, and shirube has no forecast — the composite is an allocation level with no units of expected return — so lambda * c is not computable here and the transfer is an ANALOGY (distance from neutral as a conviction proxy), not the paper's actual rule; the 0.06 gate is therefore a guess at a scale the paper cannot supply. The paper's own bootstrap tests fail to establish significant Sharpe outperformance versus buy-and-hold after multiple-testing correction, which is the same bar shirube's static-mix benchmark keeps failing, and its per-fold retraining means part of the rescued performance may come from adaptation the composite cannot do. Promotion stays gated on shirube's own Sharpe/drawdown/trade-count rule over the holdout, not on any figure above.
